edges.description: Triggered autoreactive B-cell responses feed local CNS/CSF anti-NMDAR antibody production.
Locally produced antibodies bind extracellular NR1/GluN1 epitopes on neuronal NMDA receptors.
Reduced surface and postsynaptic NMDAR availability impairs NMDAR-dependent synaptic signaling.
NMDAR hypofunction maps to the characteristic encephalitis syndrome of psychiatric symptoms, seizures, movement disorder, coma, autonomic dysfunction, and hypoventilation.
Barrier dysfunction may facilitate antibody and immune-cell traffic that sustains the intrathecal immune compartment.
Psychotic symptoms are the most frequently reported manifestation of the encephalitic syndrome and are usually what brings patients to attention.
Seizures arise from the same encephalitic network dysfunction and are co-dominant with psychosis in large cohorts.

The catatonic syndrome is produced by this encephalitic state rather than by a comorbid primary psychiatric illness. Its complete resolution with immunotherapy in every case in the cited series is the clearest argument for that direction: treating the antibody-mediated disease abolishes the catatonia.
Orolingual and limb dyskinesias are among the multivariate-selected hallmarks of the syndrome, and are more frequent in children.
Cognitive impairment, with memory among the most affected domains, is part of the syndrome and can persist after the acute illness resolves.
Speech disturbance is one of the major manifestation groups used to define the syndrome clinically, and language remains impaired long term.
Depressed consciousness up to coma occurs in severe disease as the encephalitic network dysfunction generalizes.
Autonomic instability accompanies the syndrome in about half of patients and is the feature that makes severe disease critical-care illness.
Central hypoventilation is the ventilatory component of severe disease and is one of the features that predicts functional outcome.
Mutism is one of the constituent signs of the catatonic state in this disease rather than a later complication of it; the edge records the sign as a manifestation of the state above it.
Posturing, including examiner-induced catalepsy, is likewise a constituent catatonic sign rather than a downstream sequela.

A teratoma containing neural tissue expresses NMDA receptor outside immune privilege, so the immune system meets GluN1 in a context where tolerance was never established. That is why tumour removal is part of treatment rather than merely of staging.

Reaches the same node by the opposite route to a teratoma: rather than presenting the antigen ectopically, viral destruction of neurons releases it from a privileged site. The post-herpetic form carries a poorer long-term prognosis than the idiopathic one.
An emerging candidate trigger by analogy with other post-streptococcal neuropsychiatric syndromes, but the cited evidence goes only as far as suggesting a possible infectious contribution.

Latitude and temperature correlate with incidence, which is consistent with an environmental or infectious contribution but names none. Recorded because a geographic gradient is itself a pointer to an unidentified exposure.

Diffuse slowing and epileptic discharges are the electrophysiological reading of the encephalitic network dysfunction. This is an observational readout, not a claim that the syndrome causes the tracing: generalized EEG dysfunction is one of the features that travels with the catatonic presentation.

A predominantly mononuclear CSF pleocytosis is the routine-laboratory view of the intrathecal immune compartment in which antibody synthesis occurs. It is a readout rather than a causal output: the cell count reflects the lymphocytic infiltrate, and it can be normal in patients who still have intrathecal antibody synthesis.

nodes.description: Spontaneous assumption of postures held against gravity, and catalepsy — a posture induced by an examiner and maintained. Ascertained as a core catatonic sign in this disease.

nodes.description: A psychomotor syndrome — immobility, staring, mutism and posturing predominating, with excitement often co-occurring in the same patient — present in roughly two thirds of prospectively assessed patients. It is curated as a disease in its own right in the transdiagnostic entry `Catatonia` (MONDO:0800105), whose immune-mediated hypothesis arm is anchored on this disease; what is recorded here is the frequency and sign profile specific to anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Recognising it matters clinically because catatonia is widely assumed to indicate a primary psychiatric illness, which is the route by which this encephalitis is misdiagnosed.
